1980.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":5},{"text":"You've stood here before, in a way — on before the opera and the ballet, this was San Juan Hill — a rundown, predominantly African American neighborhood of tenements that urban planner Robert Moses gleefully bulldozed in the 1960s to raise this campus.","source_id":"fc5a4288-444d-4731-838d-e0f74db24357","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Its streets got one last close-up first: the Oscar-winning gangland musical West Side Story demolition.","source_id":"fc5a4288-444d-4731-838d-e0f74db24357","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5,"also_cites":["fedecddb-340f-47fa-912e-829003caf1c9"]},{"text":"The movies never stopped tangling with this city.","source_id":"071839a1-76c4-4fe2-9c6d-bcff72e0eb74","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"In the cult musical Fame, from 1980, students from the High School of Performing Arts dance right through Midtown's streets, doing the city's traffic no favors at all.","source_id":"071839a1-76c4-4fe2-9c6d-bcff72e0eb74","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The film's content was too raw for the Board of Education, who banned shooting at the real school, then at 120 West 46th Street — so the crew used the doorway of a disused church across the street for the entrance, and Haaren Hall, at Tenth Avenue and 59th, for the interiors.","source_id":"071839a1-76c4-4fe2-9c6d-bcff72e0eb74","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"For all its ambition, the campus opened to a chorus of complaints — critics savaged its conservative design, its fortress-like walls, and its poor acoustics.","source_id":"fc5a4288-444d-4731-838d-e0f74db24357","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"So for its 50th anniversary in 2009, a $1.2-billion renovation swept through, led by the architects Diller Scofidio + Renfro and finished across 2009 and 2010 to critical acclaim.","source_id":"bd20f4cc-55a2-4c67-8892-a27d55ccf7b2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5,"also_cites":["fc5a4288-444d-4731-838d-e0f74db24357"]},{"text":"It expanded and revived a string of buildings, including Alice Tully Hall, home of the Chamber Music Society.","source_id":"bd20f4cc-55a2-4c67-8892-a27d55ccf7b2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Today Lincoln Center gathers eleven arts organizations, among them the Metropolitan Opera, the New York City Ballet, and the New York Philharmonic.","source_id":"bd20f4cc-55a2-4c67-8892-a27d55ccf7b2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"And in 2023, the music world was turned on its ear — the New York Philharmonic had stolen wunderkind conductor Gustavo Dudamel away from the Los Angeles Philharmonic.","source_id":"3fb36685-fb9c-470a-a434-9f4bac6c5510","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"It was the classical equivalent of Tom Brady abandoning Boston for Tampa.","source_id":"3fb36685-fb9c-470a-a434-9f4bac6c5510","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"His tenure opens with the 2025/26 season in the acoustically excellent, newly refurbished David Geffen Hall — the same podium Leonard Bernstein, one of the 20th century's great maestros, once commanded.","source_id":"3fb36685-fb9c-470a-a434-9f4bac6c5510","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5,"also_cites":["e1dc171e-f348-4265-b627-7ad7a2ce59a0"]},{"text":"Take a moment for the three classic buildings ringing the central Revson Fountain.","source_id":"98d67e97-c67f-47a6-929d-1019be1925ea","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The Metropolitan Opera's lobby glows with brightly saturated murals by the painter Marc Chagall; beside it stand David Geffen Hall and the David H. Koch Theater, the last designed by Philip Johnson.","source_id":"98d67e97-c67f-47a6-929d-1019be1925ea","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The Revson Fountain itself is the showstopper after dark, throwing up Las Vegas–style water shows right in the lighted plaza in front of the opera house.","source_id":"98d67e97-c67f-47a6-929d-1019be1925ea","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5,"also_cites":["91338810-d10e-4c0a-a1fd-938912cae242"]},{"text":"Step inside the Metropolitan Opera House and it's colossal — a 24-carat gold-leaf ceiling overhead and a grand staircase spiraling up through the lobby.","source_id":"91338810-d10e-4c0a-a1fd-938912cae242","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Every great voice has filled this room, from Luciano Pavarotti to Enrico Caruso to Maria Callas.","source_id":"91338810-d10e-4c0a-a1fd-938912cae242","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The repertoire runs from Verdi's Aida to Mozart's Don Giovanni — the classics, alive and well.","source_id":"e1dc171e-f348-4265-b627-7ad7a2ce59a0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"But New York's real gift to the stage might be dance — for nearly a century, this city has sat at the center of it.","source_id":"50e06985-c479-476f-98d4-d632ecac87c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The American Ballet Theatre, founded in 1939 by Lucia Chase and Richard Pleasant, set out to grow homegrown talent, staging works by Jerome Robbins, Twyla Tharp, and Alvin Ailey.","source_id":"50e06985-c479-476f-98d4-d632ecac87c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"And the city nurtured the rule-breakers too — Martha Graham, who traded grace for boxy, industrial movement on bare, almost abstract sets, and Merce Cunningham, who cut dance loose from music entirely.","source_id":"50e06985-c479-476f-98d4-d632ecac87c6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"And that brings our walk to a close.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Thank you for coming along with me today. When you're ready, take your time and keep exploring on your own.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":5}]}
